configuration.SAS.flowConversionModeSwim: Convert each notebook cell to a swimlane
configuration.SAS.log.clearOnExecutionSt: Clear SAS Log when code execution starts
configuration.SAS.log.showOnExecutionFin: Show SAS Log when code execution is finished
configuration.SAS.log.showOnExecutionSta: Show SAS Log when code execution starts
configuration.SAS.notebook.export.includ: Include SAS log in exported notebook
configuration.SAS.console.logOutput: Positron only: the parts of the SAS log that the SAS console shows. Errors and warnings are still counted, and the console always shows the error summary. The **SAS Log** output channel always has the full log. The command **SAS: Choose Console Log Output** changes this setting.
configuration.SAS.dataFiles.openWith: Positron 2026.12 and later: what a double-click on a `.sas7bdat` or `.xpt` file opens. Positron opens these files in its own Data Explorer without a SAS session. With a SAS session running, the extension can reopen them through the session, which shows SAS formats and reads `PROC CPORT` files and transport files with several datasets; Positron reads the file first, so large files take longer. To always open them through SAS, set `workbench.editorAssociations` instead: `"*.sas7bdat": "sas.sas7bdatViewer"`.
configuration.SAS.dataFiles.openWith.sas: Through the SAS session while one is running; otherwise in Positron's Data Explorer
configuration.SAS.dataFiles.openWith.pos: Always in Positron's Data Explorer; use Open with SAS to open a file through the SAS session
configuration.SAS.console.logOutput.sour: The SAS code echoed in the log, with line numbers
configuration.SAS.console.logOutput.note: NOTE lines and other log text
configuration.SAS.audit.logFile: Positron only: file that records every SAS console submission (user, session, code and outcome) as JSON Lines, for audit and traceability. `~` expands to the home directory. Leave empty to turn auditing off.
configuration.SAS.variablesPane.enabled: Positron only: show the SAS console's GLOBAL and AUTOMATIC macro variables and WORK datasets in the Variables pane. The pane is updated after each submission with one extra query (on SAS Viya, through the Compute API without running SAS code).
configuration.SAS.session.keepAliveSecon: SAS Viya connections: how often, in seconds, the extension contacts an idle SAS session so that the server does not end it for inactivity. Set to `0` to turn this off. Pinging stops after 8 hours without a submit.
configuration.SAS.localSasPaths: Positron only: extra locations of a local SAS launcher (fully qualified paths), checked before the built-in SAS Analytics Pro and SAS 9.4 locations and `sas` on `PATH`. The first executable one becomes the `local` stdio connection profile, which is added once when no stdio profile exists.

commands.SAS.backgroundJobs.chooseComput: Choose Compute Context for Background Jobs...
configuration.SAS.backgroundJobs.compute: The SAS Viya compute context that background jobs run in. When empty, background jobs use the `context` of the active connection profile, or `SAS Job Execution compute context`, the same as interactive runs.
configuration.SAS.backgroundJobs.keepRes: How long SAS Viya keeps a finished background job, as an ISO-8601 duration such as `P7D` (seven days) or `PT12H` (twelve hours). When it expires, the server deletes the job **together with its log and listing**.
Enter an ISO-8601 duration, such as P7D or PT12H.
lsaf.views.signIn.welcome:
Sign in to SAS Life Science Analytics Framework (LSAF) to browse its repository and your workspace and run jobs.
[Sign In](command:SAS.lsaf.signIn)
lsaf.views.jobs.welcome:
Jobs you run from Positron appear here. Run a job with Run Job on a .job file, or a program with Run on LSAF on a .sas file in the workspace.
The LSAF REST API can't list runs, so jobs started elsewhere don't appear.
configuration.SAS.lsaf.url: URL of a SAS Life Science Analytics Framework (LSAF) server, such as `https://lsaf.example.com` or its REST API `https://lsaf.example.com/lsaf/api`. The LSAF views appear when this server answers like LSAF. When empty, the `SAS_LSAF_URL` environment variable is used.
configuration.SAS.lsaf.userId: The LSAF user ID suggested when signing in.
